pr_body:
A constant value can be converted to a specified type during analysis, not at runtime every time.

```gdscript
var x: StringName = 'a' # initializer

x = 'b' # assignment

func print_name(y: StringName): print(y)
print_name('c') # call argument

func make_name() -> StringName: return 'd' # return

var z := 'c' as StringName # cast
```

Out of those places only variable initializer was handled at compile time before. 

Initializer for constants was not converted at all which was leading to many crash reports.

While at it, allowed a cast to be considered as constant expression under certain circumstances (which will be expanded with array PR from which code for this PR partially comes from).

Fixed minor things with casts and arguments validations.

Fixes #70861.
Fixes #71255.
Fixes #71483.
Fixes #71635.
Fixes #72209.

Related to #70872 (supersedes).
Related to #70873 (supersedes).
pr_comments: This PR does not fully supersede #70873, as there are more changes to `resolve_assignable()`, not just the part that can be replaced by `update_const_expression_builtin_type()` call. (I will rebase #70873 after this PR is merged.)

I looked now and assume that the thing that wasn't included here was a correction for wrong check of compatibility when it comes to asymmetric conversions  - String can be converted to Color, but other way around will never work. 

It can be fixed by disallowing implicit conversions in reverse check (reverse check is done only to allow cases where variable of class type is used where subclass is expected, since those are objects no implicit conversions should take place). Updated the PR and fixed the same mistake in usual assignments too.

Is there anything else that is missing?

> Is there anything else that is missing?

1. Some tests are missing.
2. I think in my PR the code has been reorganized to be more readable: first the status is determined (`SAFE`, `UNSAFE`, `ERROR`) and then actions are performed depending on this. This can help avoid mistakes in the future.
Needs another rebase to pass CI, I fixed the GDScript test error.

```
extends Node3D
# backgound unit is 1km or 1000m
const backgroundCameraNear : float = 100.0
const backgroundCameraFar : float = 100000.0
const backgroundResolution : int = 1024*2
var spinner : int = 0
const viewportNames : PackedStringArray = ["Front", "Left", "Right", "Back", "Up", "Down"]
var viewports : Array

var spinnerSkips : int = 240

func _ready():
	var backgroundWorld : World3D = $BackgroundFront.get_viewport().world_3d
	for viewportName in viewportNames:
		setupDirectionalViewport(backgroundWorld, viewportName)

func _process(_delta):
	spinner += 1
	if 0 == spinner % spinnerSkips:
		for viewport in viewports:
			viewport.set_update_mode(SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE)

func setupDirectionalViewport(backgroundWorld : World3D, direction : String):
	var backgroundViewport : SubViewport = get_node("Background" + direction)
	viewports.append(backgroundViewport)
	#Make all background viewports instances of the same world
	backgroundViewport.get_viewport().world_3d = backgroundWorld
	backgroundViewport.size = Vector2i(backgroundResolution, backgroundResolution)
	#Make all camera settings equal
	var backgroundCamera : Camera3D = backgroundViewport.get_node(direction + "Camera")
	backgroundCamera.near = backgroundCameraNear
	backgroundCamera.far = backgroundCameraFar

```

I can't bisect using official builds, as the project needs custom modules to run. (but none of the custom modules override standard modules or are used/called/referenced at all in this crashing GDScript).
Removing PackedStringArray type hint fixes the problem for me. Is this still a bug, or this was somehow missuse of packed array?
I'm pretty sure that this is for #70873.

review_comments: I'm not sure if a silent return here is correct. It seems to me that either `ERR_FAIL_COND` is needed here, or the method should return `bool`.

This is not an error case, if an expected type is not built-in or enum (so a variant or an object) then there is nothing to do - no conversion will take place. There are checks afterwards in all corresponding places (where the method is used) that deal with checking that types do match. 

Usage of the method assumes that you call it before storing the resulting type of an expression or its reduced value, like `update_array_literal_element_type`, `const_fold` and `reduce_expression`, no need to return booleans.
